adjudication: Three independent readers agreed EXACTLY on the accent layer: 6 anudatta + 5 svarita = 11, with identical (word_index, aksara_index, type) tuples for all 11 marks (verified programmatically). One aksara identity was disputed: word 1 aksara 0, read HYA by R1, HA by R2, A by R3 - a 1-1-1 split with no majority. ADJUDICATED FROM THE SCAN: (a) the conjunct reading HYA is RULED OUT on width. R1, R2 and R3 each independently measured this aksara at 79-83 px. R2's on-line controls give 82 px for the single consonant CA and 114-120 px for every consonant+YA conjunct on the same line (SYA 114 px, M+YA 120 px), because this fount always writes YA with its own crescent counter and stem. An adjudicator body-band column profile confirms the word occupies x575-783 with the aksara break at ~662-670, i.e. 88 px + 114 px. (b) Between HA and A the 2024 px raster does not settle it. 2 of 3 readers (R1, R2) saw HA-based ink. The adjudicator composited the glyph against a certain A and a certain HA from canvas 32 line 19 (a line already settled by readers Q1/Q2), and found the disputed glyph's left element to be a rounded curl with an inner hook and a down-right tail - the HA structure - rather than the angular two-lobe form of the certain A. HA is adopted as the majority-supported reading with R1's subjoined YA removed on the width evidence. R3's A reading is preserved as recorded dissent and the aksara remains flagged unclear. This locus provably does not affect any gate metric: all three readings yield identical mark tuples, because HYA, HA and A are all a single aksara cluster in position 0.
boundary_interpretation: WORD BOUNDARIES. I projected column ink over the sirorekha band (y 1031-1044) and over the whole line (y 995-1130). The headline is continuous inside a word and breaks only between words, by 35-49 px. That gives ten word runs plus the tail punctuation, in block-x: 341-534, 575-783, 822-1110, 1149-1383, 1422-1661, 1698-1787, 1828-2065, 2107-2124 (the single danda, only 18 px wide), 2166-2437, 2472-2922; then 2984-3001 and 3007-3025 (a double danda), 3050-3116 (the verse numeral), 3142-3181 (a second double danda). The decisive check is that 2472-2922 is one unbroken 451 px headline covering five aksaras, which proves the 40-49 px breaks are word breaks and not aksara breaks. WORD INDEXING. word_index counts Devanagari words only, left to right: 0 eva, 1 hyasya, 2 kamya, 3 stoma, 4 uktham, 5 ca, 6 shamsya, 7 indraya, 8 somapitaye. The single danda, the double dandas and the numeral are NOT counted as words; if a comparer counts the single danda as a token, add 1 to my indices 7 and 8. AKSARA BOUNDARIES came from a second column projection restricted to the body band y 1050-1126, where aksaras inside a word do separate: eva 348-416 / 428-523; hyasya 580-661 / 670-774; kamya 829-938 / 953-1099; stoma 1158-1291 / 1305-1375; uktham 1430-1495 / 1509-1652; shamsya 1834-1903 / 1912-2053; indraya 2175-2323 (the initial i and the ndra cluster touch at body level) / 2336-2354 (the aa stem) / 2372-2431; somapitaye 2474-2582 / 2586-2665 / 2681-2772 / 2789-2844 / 2859-2917. MARKS NEAR A BOUNDARY, and how I resolved each. (a) svarita x 648 in hyasya sits 13 px inside the first aksara (580-661) and 22 px clear of the second (starts 670), so aksara 0. It stands directly over a stem that continues below the headline at exactly the same x (641-655), and that stem belongs to aksara 0. (b) anudatta x 752 (bar 734-771) lies wholly inside 670-774, aksara 1 of hyasya, 64 px right of the aksara break; unambiguous. (c) anudatta x 1040 (bar 1021-1059) lies wholly inside the second aksara of kamya (953-1099), 68 px right of the break at 938/953; unambiguous. (d) svarita x 1361 (1356-1367) lies inside the ma of stoma (1305-1375), over the right stem of ma, 8 px from its right edge but 55 px from the next word (headline starts 1422); assigned to ma, aksara 1. (e) anudatta x 1479 (bar 1461-1497) is centred under the initial u (1430-1495) and stops 12 px before the next aksara starts at 1509; assigned to u, aksara 0. This is the only bar whose right edge just crosses an aksara break, but its centre and the bulk of its ink sit under u. (f) svarita x 2652 (2646-2658) sits inside the ma of somapitaye (2586-2665), over the right stem of ma, 13 px from its right edge and 23 px before pa starts at 2681; assigned to ma, aksara 1 (so=0, ma=1, pii=2, ta=3, ye=4). (g) in indraya the initial i ends near x 2230 in the rendered glyph, so svarita x 2304 is over the ndra cluster, above its n/d stem: aksara 1. anudatta x 2407 (2389-2426) is wholly inside the final ya (2372-2431): aksara 2. (h) anudatta x 1759 (1741-1778) sits under ca, a one-aksara word (1710-1777): aksara 0. (i) anudatta x 362 (bar 344-380) sits under the initial e (348-416), 48 px before va starts at 428: aksara 0 of eva.
dissent: Read word 1 aksara 0 as HYA (ha + subjoined ya), from a mid-height left spur on the stem. OVERRULED: 79-83 px is the single-consonant width class on this line; consonant+ya is 114-120 px.
notes: MAGNIFICATION. I started from the two supplied 1568 px segments (about 1:1 with the 2024 px native scan). Because the raster carries no further detail, I then worked mainly by direct measurement of the source image with PIL - row-ink profiles, column-ink profiles and 8-connected component bounding boxes - and used self-rendered LANCZOS crops of the same line at about 2.6x, 5.2-6.0x and 6.45x only to check the SHAPE of each candidate against its measured box. Every x and y quoted is in leaf-block coordinates, which for this line are identical to global line-x: the line spans the full 3216 px block width, so seg1_x/0.9469 and 1560 + seg2_x/0.9469 both recover block-x. ACCEPTED MARKS. Six anudatta: the only components in my bar band y 1134-1146 are 344-380, 734-771, 1021-1059, 1461-1497, 1741-1778 and 2389-2426, all 37-39 px wide and 10-12 px tall, i.e. flat dashes inside the stated 20-45 by 5-18 profile. A 4-pixel-minimum component sweep over the wider window y 1128-1170 found no seventh candidate. Five svarita: 642-654, 1356-1367, 1997-2007, 2299-2309 and 2646-2658, all 11-13 px wide and 33-34 px tall, standing clear above the sirorekha (top edge 1029) with their upper ends at y 993-1007. REJECTED, WITH THE SHAPE REASON. (1) The line-ABOVE (line 4) anudatta band at y 961-975, blobs centred at x 362, 759, 990, 1030, 1255, 1609, 2110, 2312, 2672 and 2790. Rejected because they lie one full line pitch (172 px) above my own bar band and are cut off from my svarita band by rows 976-994, which carry ZERO ink across all 3216 columns. Two are deliberately seductive: x 2312 sits directly above my genuine svarita at 2304, and x 362 directly above my genuine bar at 362. Shape separates them too - they are 35-39 by 11-12 dashes, not 11-13 by 33 strokes. (2) Anusvara dots, rejected as svarita: x 1628-1650 (23 by 25 px, over the ktham of uktham) and x 1881-1901 (21 by 24 px, over the sham of shamsya). Both are round or diamond blobs about as wide as tall, and at 5.9x they are visibly lozenges rather than strokes. This is the discrimination that fixes the fount for me: shamsya carries BOTH a round dot (1891) and an upright stroke (2002) inside one word, so the two glyphs are certainly distinct in this print. (3) Wide curved matras above the headline: 1215-1285 (71 px, the o of sto), 2509-2580 (72 px, the o of so), 2711-2769 (59 px, the long i of pii) and 2851-2911 (61 px, the e of ye). All 59-72 px across and visibly hooked, far wider than the 6-16 px svarita. (4) x 1504-1571, 68 by 2 px at y 1027-1028: the top edge of the sirorekha under the ktha, only two rows tall. Also several one-row slivers at y 1028 (x 347-356, 671-674, 1044-1052, 1156-1159, 1210-1216, 1482-1485), all headline top edge. (5) x 3059-3095, 37 by 22 px at y 1007-1028: the upper lobe of the verse numeral, wider than tall and continuous with the numeral body below the headline. (6) x 3103-3109, 7 by 3 px at y 1124-1126: the tip of the numeral's descending tail. Too small for a bar, above my bar band, and running continuously into the numeral with no white gap. (7) Line 4 curled ink at x 973-1037 y 958-969 and at x 2762-2818 y 958-975: curved hooks and curls (the second is 57 by 18), not straight dashes, and in the line-above band in any case. (8) The subscript ra of the ndra in indraya, a curved hook around x 2284-2322, y 1080-1120: it sits inside my body band, well above the bar band at 1134, and it is a hook rather than a dash. (9) No danda slice contaminates either band. The single danda (x 2107-2124) and the double dandas (2984-3001, 3007-3025, 3142-3181) all lie between the sirorekha and the body floor and never enter y 993-1028 or y 1134-1146. READING PROBLEMS. (a) Word 3 is printed stoma with NO anusvara. Above its final ma there is only the 12 by 34 upright stroke at 1356-1367; at 6.45x there is no round dot, and the 38 px gap to the next word (1384-1421) is completely blank, so no dot sits outside the cluster either. My memory of the Atharvaveda wants stomam here, and in the 1568 px segment I did at first misread this svarita as an anusvara. The ink does not support an anusvara, so I follow the ink: stoma carrying a svarita. (b) unclear_count = 1, namely the first aksara of word 1. At 2024 px I cannot cleanly separate hya (half-ha plus ya) from ha plus an aa-matra: the cluster is 82 px wide (580-661) against 105 px for the sya that follows, and I read the mid-height left spur on its stem as ya, giving hyasya. Either way the mark at x 648 belongs to aksara 0 of that word, so the accent attribution does not depend on the choice. (c) The verse numeral reads 6, a two-lobed figure with a descending tail. I am confident, but it is a single 67 px glyph and I record it as read. (d) Per the fount note I checked the two initial vowels: x 1430-1495 is u (not a), and x 2165-2230 is i. No standalone a occurs on this line, so the ri/shra confusion the note warns about does not arise here.
